quizzes.question: Why did Pope Hadrian call on Charles for help in 773?
options: Byzantine armies had landed in Italy
Muslim forces had crossed the Pyrenees
quizzes.explanation: Charles beat the Lombards and then took their crown for himself. The lands he handed to the Church afterwards bound papacy and Frankish throne together for centuries.

quizzes.question: What title did Pope Leo III give Charles on Christmas Day, 800?
quizzes.explanation: He was the first ruler in western Europe to carry an imperial title since Rome fell. In Constantinople, where a real Roman emperor still sat, the coronation was read as an insult.

quizzes.question: What became of the empire after the death of Charles's son Louis the Pious?
options: It passed whole to one grandson
Louis's three sons divided it between them
The Pope took it under his rule
It was conquered by the Saxons
quizzes.explanation: Frankish custom split inheritances, the same custom that had once forced Charles to share with his brother Carloman. This time no brother died early to undo the division.

polls.question: The Saxon wars ran for more than thirty years. What do you think kept them going so long?
options: The Saxons would not give up their religion
The land was too wide to hold

polls.question: Which of Charles's works do you think mattered most to his empire?
options: Counts and bishops answerable to him

polls.question: Why did the empire not outlive its builder?
options: No successor had his force of will
It was always too large to govern

choices.prompt: Carloman's death left Charles sole ruler, and he drove his brother's widow and children into exile. In his place, what would you have done?
options: Keep them at court under watch

choices.prompt: In his seventies Charles still rode with his armies and shared their hardships. In his place, what would you have done?
options: Send an heir in your name
